issues.where: Status claim 'The data download is still running and should take about 30 minutes'; runs/logs/fetch.log; data/human/GRCh38.primary_assembly.genome.fa.gz
issues.problem: The claim is false. No curl, fetch.sh or setup.sh process is running in WSL: ps and pgrep found none at 11:44-11:46. data/human/GRCh38.primary_assembly.genome.fa.gz has been stuck at 93,711,360 bytes since 11:43:51, a fraction of the roughly 0.9 GB file. The last line of fetch.log is the human MD5SUMS ('got ... MD5SUMS local=2797 server=2797'), with no 'got', 'SIZE MISMATCH' or 'downloads done' after it. The mouse, zebrafish and mosquito folders are empty, and fly holds only its two CHECKSUMS files. The download died without logging anything, so no completion notification will arrive. The '30 minutes' figure is not supported by anything either.
issues.fix: Restart env/fetch.sh detached so it survives the wsl.exe call returning: setsid nohup bash /mnt/e/.../env/fetch.sh >> runs/logs/fetch.log 2>&1 &, or the harness's run_in_background. Add 'exec 2>>$LOG' (or 2>&1 on curl) so curl errors reach the log. Confirm the file keeps growing and the process still exists before reporting that it is running. Drop the time estimate, or base it on the measured transfer rate.

issues.problem: fetch.sh says it verifies 'against server size and published checksums', but it only compares sizes. The MD5 and BSD sum checks are in env/setup.sh. If fetch.sh is run alone, as it was here, nothing has been checked against a checksum, and the partial GRCh38 file currently on disk has not been verified at all.
issues.fix: Change the comment to 'server size only', or call the checksum block at the end of fetch.sh. Either way, the report must cite runs/logs/setup.log showing 'md5 OK' or 'sum OK' for all 9 data files plus the k8 md5 and paftools sha256 before any number is used.
